newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CANTONA PRAISES NEW NORWEGIAN STRIKER SOLSKJAER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CANTONA PRAISES NEW NORWEGIAN STRIKER SOLSKJAER.

text.p: Manchester United skipper Eric Cantona says his new Norwegian teammate Ole Solskjaer has the ice-cool scoring instincts of his old French strike partner Jean-Pierre Papin.

The 23-year-old scored his fourth goal in six games as Manchester United beat Rapid Vienna 2-0 in the Champions League on Wednesday and Cantona said: "He is very good, he has such very quick feet and he reminds me of Jean-Pierre Papin when I used to play with him. It's important to have a player like him."

Solskjaer, inititially bought as an investment for the future, cost a relatively modest 1.5 million pounds ($2.34 million) from Norwegian club Molde and United manager Alex Ferguson enthused: "He improves almost every week.

"This was another big step up for him. It's amazing to think that two years ago he was playing some minor football in Norway, equivalent to third or fourth division standard. You've got to think there's a lot more to come from him the way he is improving. He's very quick about the box and prepared to hit things other players may be only think about."
Solskjaer said: "If I get the chance, I'll always have a shot you can't be afraid if you're a striker.
"It wasn't a difficult goal to score, but it's a goal all the same. But I should have had two more."
But it was not all joy for United, who marked their fourth decade in Europe with their 56th unbeaten match at home.
Their celebrations were clouded by an ankle injury to Solskjaer's compatriot Ronny Johnsen which could put him out for up to a month.
